title: Number of Bit Changes to Make Two Integers Equal
description: You are given two non-negative integers `n` and `k`. In one operation, you may choose any bit in the binary representation of `n` that is currently equal to `1` and change it to `0` (you cannot change a `0` bit to `1`). Return the minimum number of operations needed to make `n` equal to `k`, or `-1` if it is impossible.
hints: Since you can only clear `1` bits to `0`, every `1` bit in `k` must already be a `1` bit in `n`, which holds if and only if `(n & k) == k`.
When `(n & k) == k`, the exact number of bits that must be cleared is the population count of `n ^ k`.

examples.explanation: 13 is 1101 and 4 is 0100 in binary; clearing bits 3 and 0 takes 2 changes.
14 is 1110 and 13 is 1101; bit 0 is 0 in 14 but 1 in 13, so it is impossible.
